about: Published figures on Indian political parties and leaders on Instagram, each traced to the report that printed it. Read by /instagram-politics. Figures are as the source states them; nothing here is estimated or filled in. Where sources disagree, both are kept. Accessed through search excerpts on 2026-10-20: the article pages could not be opened from the editing environment, so each figure carries the sentence it was read from.

engagementBeforeAfterJuly20.method: Data Beings, a social-listening firm: average engagement per post on Instagram before and after 20 July 2026, the CJP's march to Parliament.

rows.quote: His average engagement per post rose from 1.19 million before July 20 to 4.63 million afterwards, representing a 289.9% increase.

rows.notes: The article's sentence says followers; the study measures engagement per post, and a party with 13 million followers cannot have 50,000. Read as engagement per post.

context.text: CJP passes Congress and the BJP to become the most-followed party account on Instagram, about a week after launch.
Dipke says the CJP website was taken down and the Instagram account hacked; Reuters could not verify a government takedown.
The CJP's march to Parliament; Data Beings' before-and-after split for Modi, Rahul Gandhi, the BJP and Congress.
Jantar Mantar protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar: 500 to 700 detained, including AAP's Atishi and AISA's Neha Bora.
Aaj Tak opinion: "why there was no vibe at the protest this time".
